matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks meeting) can be turned into an X (two crossing diagonals) by moving one of its sticks to cross the other, changing its value by +5; conversely, moving a stick from an X to make a V reduces the value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a multiple of 5 and a V or X appears that can be altered without breaking other characters.
matchstick.example: IV = XIV - V → move one diagonal of the right‑most V to cross the other diagonal, turning it into X and yielding IV = XIV - X, which balances (4 = 14‑10).

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides of the equation; the difference indicates how much the total must change, pointing to likely numeral adjustments (e.g., a difference of 5 suggests a V↔X change).
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of any matchstick‑roman puzzle, before considering specific stick moves.
matchstick.example: IV = XIV - V gives 4 on the left and 9 on the right, a discrepancy of 5, suggesting a V↔X conversion.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The ‘=’ sign must remain as two horizontal sticks; moving a stick from or to it would break the required equality operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process; treat ‘=’ as immutable.
matchstick.example: Do not remove a horizontal line from ‘=’ or add a third line to it.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, every numeral and operator must still be a valid Roman numeral or arithmetic symbol; no leftover single diagonal or missing line is allowed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V to make X is valid because the V becomes X; moving it away entirely would leave an invalid single diagonal.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved from one part of a character to another part of the same character, effectively changing its shape (e.g., repositioning a V’s stick to cross the other creates an X).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a needed transformation involves only one character and no external stick source is available.
matchstick.example: In the right‑most V, relocate one diagonal so it crosses the other, turning the V into an X.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a vertical stick cannot be used as a diagonal and vice‑versa. Moves must respect the required orientation of the target shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When selecting which stick to move and where to place it.
matchstick.example: You cannot take a diagonal stick from an X and use it to form an I, which requires a vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator (e.g., ‘-’ to ‘+’) requires adding or removing sticks in a way that leaves both the source and target operators valid; otherwise the equation is malformed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When contemplating moving a stick from or to an operator.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘-’ (one horizontal) into ‘+’ needs a vertical stick from elsewhere, but the source must still be a valid operator after removal.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any candidate stick move, recalculate the Roman‑numeral values to verify that the equality now holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each plausible transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After converting the right‑most V to X, compute XIV ‑ X = 14 ‑ 10 = 4, which matches IV = 4.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as generic pieces and ignores that vertical, horizontal, and diagonal sticks are not interchangeable.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce orientation constraints: only move a stick to a position that requires the same orientation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model thinks any character can be altered to adjust values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat ‘=’ as immutable; never move a stick from or to it.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model does not check that the source numeral remains a valid Roman numeral after a stick is removed.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every numeral and operator still matches a known Roman‑numeral shape.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: Attempting to adjust the equation by turning ‘-’ into nothing or turning ‘=’ into ‘≠’ without preserving operator validity.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only perform operator changes that result in a recognized operator and keep the original operator valid after removal.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks arbitrarily without a guiding numeric target.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Start by computing the numeric difference between sides; use that to decide which numeral’s value should be altered.
